# Chain Guide and Chain Tensioner for Lubricated Sliding Systems

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a chain guide or chain tensioner specifically engineered for use within lubricated sliding systems. These components are characterized by an integrated surface layer, bearing, or sliding element that has been optimized to withstand the demanding thermal and mechanical conditions encountered in modern power train applications.

## Composition of the Surface Layer

The surface layer forming the functional interface of the chain guide or chain tensioner is fundamentally constructed from a polymeric material. This polymeric material comprises a matrix polymer as its principal structural component, though it may optionally incorporate additional dispersed phases. These dispersed components can include fillers, reinforcing agents, lubricating additives, or other functional materials that are distributed throughout the polymer matrix to enhance specific performance characteristics such as wear resistance, thermal stability, or friction reduction.

## Matrix Polymer Specification

Central to the invention is the specific selection of the matrix polymer, which is defined as a semi-crystalline polyamide (SCPA). This polymer is distinguished by its mechanical performance at elevated temperatures, specifically exhibiting a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa when measured at 140°C in accordance with the ISO 527-1A standard. This particular thermal-mechanical property ensures that the material retains sufficient structural rigidity and dimensional stability under the high-temperature conditions typically encountered within automotive engine and transmission environments, where lubricated chain systems are commonly deployed.

## Power Train Drive System Integration

The scope of the invention further extends to a complete power train drive system that incorporates the chain guide or chain tensioner described above. This drive system comprises several interconnected components, including:

- An engine as the primary power source
- A transmission differential for power distribution
- A drive shaft system for mechanical power transfer
- A drive chain that transmits rotational force
- A plastic component featuring a sliding element that maintains direct contact with the lubricated drive chain

This integrated system architecture ensures that the specialized polymeric sliding element functions effectively within the broader mechanical context of the power train, providing reliable performance throughout the operational life of the vehicle or machinery.

## Frictional Performance Characteristics

A key performance attribute of the chain guide, chain tensioner, or sliding element disclosed in this invention is its exceptionally low coefficient of friction (CoF). Specifically, the material achieves a CoF of at most 0.07 under standardized testing conditions that closely simulate real-world operating environments. These test conditions include:

- Measurement within lubrication oil
- A testing temperature of 140°C
- A nominal contact pressure of 1 MPa
- A sliding speed of 1 m/s

This low-friction performance, maintained even under elevated temperature and pressure conditions, represents a significant advantage for applications requiring efficient power transmission, reduced energy losses, minimized wear, and extended component service life within lubricated chain drive systems.

# Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to polymeric materials suitable for use in sliding applications within power train systems, and more particularly to sliding elements such as chain guides and chain tensioners that operate in contact with lubricated drive chains under demanding thermal and mechanical conditions.

# Background of the Invention

Chain guides and chain tensioners are critical components in power train drive systems, including automotive engines, transmissions, and industrial machinery. These components must maintain low friction against a moving chain while withstanding elevated temperatures generated during operation, particularly in environments lubricated with hot engine or transmission oil. Conventional polymeric materials used for these applications often suffer from a significant loss of mechanical stiffness at elevated temperatures, leading to increased friction, accelerated wear, and reduced component lifespan. There exists a continuing need in the art for improved materials that retain sufficient mechanical properties at high operating temperatures while simultaneously providing low friction characteristics when in contact with lubricated chains.

# Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these shortcomings by providing a surface layer formed from a polymeric material comprising a matrix of semi-crystalline polyamide (SCPA). The SCPA matrix is specifically selected or formulated to exhibit a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa when measured at 140°C, ensuring that the material retains substantial mechanical rigidity even under the elevated temperature conditions typically encountered in power train environments.

This SCPA-based polymeric material is particularly suited for incorporation into sliding elements, such as chain guides and chain tensioners, that are designed to operate in direct contact with a lubricated drive chain within a power train drive system. When implemented in such applications, the sliding element formed from this material achieves a notably low coefficient of friction—specifically, a coefficient of friction of at most 0.07—under conditions of high-temperature oil lubrication.

This combination of high-temperature mechanical stability and low friction performance represents a significant advancement over conventional materials used in chain guide and tensioner applications. By maintaining a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa at 140°C, the SCPA matrix resists deformation and wear that would otherwise compromise the sliding interface between the guide or tensioner and the chain. Simultaneously, the achievement of a coefficient of friction at or below 0.07 under lubricated, high-temperature conditions ensures smooth chain movement, reduced energy losses, and minimized heat generation at the sliding interface.

# Detailed Description

## The SCPA Matrix Material

The semi-crystalline polyamide employed in the polymeric material of the present invention may be selected from a range of polyamide types known to exhibit semi-crystalline morphology, including but not limited to polyamide 6 (PA6), polyamide 66 (PA66), polyamide 46 (PA46), polyamide 610, polyamide 612, and various copolyamides thereof. The selection of the specific SCPA, as well as any modifications through additives, reinforcing fillers, or blending with other polymeric components, is guided by the requirement that the resulting matrix maintain a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa at 140°C, as measured according to standard tensile testing methods.

The semi-crystalline nature of the polyamide is significant in that it contributes to dimensional stability and mechanical strength retention at elevated temperatures, as the crystalline domains within the polymer matrix resist thermal softening more effectively than amorphous regions. This property is essential for applications in which the sliding element is exposed to oil temperatures that may reach or exceed 140°C during normal engine or transmission operation.

## Formulation Considerations

In certain embodiments, the SCPA matrix may be reinforced with fibrous or particulate fillers, such as glass fibers, carbon fibers, or mineral fillers, to further enhance the tensile modulus and overall mechanical performance of the material at elevated temperatures. Additionally, the polymeric material may incorporate lubricating additives, internal lubricants, or friction-reducing agents dispersed within the SCPA matrix to further lower the coefficient of friction at the sliding interface without compromising the structural integrity of the material.

The proportion of reinforcing fillers, if present, may range from a few percent to a substantial fraction of the total composition by weight, depending on the desired balance between mechanical stiffness, toughness, and processability. The formulation may be optimized through routine experimentation to achieve the specified tensile modulus threshold while maintaining suitable properties for injection molding or other manufacturing processes commonly used to produce chain guides and tensioners.

## Sliding Element Configuration

The sliding element of the present invention comprises a surface layer formed from the SCPA-based polymeric material described above, which is positioned to make direct contact with the drive chain during operation. This surface layer may constitute the entirety of the sliding element or may be applied as a coating or overlay on a substrate formed from a different material, such as a metal or a different polymeric composition, depending on the specific design requirements of the chain guide or tensioner.

The geometry of the sliding element, including the contour of the sliding surface, may be tailored to match the specific chain type and power train configuration in which it is employed. Common configurations include curved guide rails, tensioner arms, and pivoting shoe elements, each of which relies on the low-friction, high-temperature-stable properties of the SCPA matrix to ensure reliable performance over extended service intervals.

## Performance Under Lubricated Conditions

A key aspect of the present invention is the performance of the sliding element under conditions of high-temperature oil lubrication, which is representative of the operating environment found in many automotive and industrial power train systems. Under such conditions, the sliding element achieves a coefficient of friction of at most 0.07, as measured through standard friction testing protocols involving a lubricated chain in sliding contact with the polymeric surface layer at elevated oil temperatures.

This low coefficient of friction translates directly into reduced energy consumption within the power train system, as less mechanical energy is dissipated as heat at the sliding interface between the chain and the guide or tensioner. Additionally, the reduced friction contributes to decreased wear rates for both the sliding element and the chain itself, thereby extending the operational lifespan of the power train components and reducing the frequency of maintenance or replacement.

## Advantages Over Conventional Materials

Conventional polymeric materials used in chain guide and tensioner applications often fail to maintain adequate mechanical properties at elevated temperatures, resulting in increased deformation, higher friction, and accelerated wear under the thermal conditions typical of modern power train systems. The present invention overcomes these limitations by specifically selecting and formulating an SCPA matrix that retains a tensile modulus of at least 800 MPa at 140°C, thereby ensuring that the sliding element maintains its structural integrity and dimensional stability even under sustained high-temperature operation.

Furthermore, the achievement of a coefficient of friction of at most 0.07 under lubricated conditions represents a substantial improvement over many conventional materials, which often exhibit higher friction coefficients that lead to increased energy losses and accelerated component wear. This combination of properties makes the SCPA-based polymeric material of the present invention particularly well-suited for use in modern power train drive systems, where efficiency, durability, and reliability are of paramount importance.

## Applications

The sliding elements formed from the SCPA-based polymeric material of the present invention may be employed in a wide variety of power train drive systems, including but not limited to automotive engines, automatic and manual transmissions, motorcycle drive systems, and industrial chain drive applications. The invention is particularly advantageous in systems where the chain guide or tensioner is exposed to hot lubricating oil, such as engine timing chain systems, where oil temperatures can reach levels sufficient to compromise the performance of conventional polymeric materials.

By providing a sliding element that maintains both high-temperature mechanical stability and low-friction performance, the present invention enables the design of more efficient, durable, and reliable chain guide and tensioner components for use across a broad range of power train applications.

# Understanding SCPA and Pressure Measurements in MPa

The Standard for Compressive Pressure Assessment (SCPA) serves as an important benchmark in materials engineering and quality control processes across various industries, including construction, manufacturing, and geotechnical engineering. This framework establishes standardized procedures for testing and evaluating the strength characteristics of materials, ensuring consistency and reliability in measurements taken across different laboratories and testing facilities.

At the core of SCPA testing lies the measurement unit MPa, or megapascal, which represents one million pascals of pressure. This unit has become the international standard for expressing compressive strength, tensile strength, and other mechanical properties of materials such as concrete, steel, and various composite materials. The use of MPa allows engineers and scientists worldwide to communicate results in a universally understood format, eliminating confusion that might arise from regional variations in measurement systems.

The relationship between SCPA protocols and MPa measurements is fundamental to quality assurance in construction and manufacturing. When materials undergo testing according to SCPA guidelines, the resulting values—typically expressed in MPa—provide critical information about whether a material meets required specifications for its intended application. For instance, concrete used in structural applications might need to achieve a minimum compressive strength of 25 to 40 MPa, depending on the specific requirements of the project.

The importance of following SCPA standards cannot be overstated, as deviations from proper testing procedures can lead to inaccurate MPa readings, potentially compromising structural integrity and safety. Laboratories that adhere to SCPA protocols typically employ calibrated equipment and controlled environmental conditions to ensure that the MPa values obtained are both accurate and reproducible.

Furthermore, the integration of SCPA methodologies with MPa measurements has facilitated international trade and collaboration in engineering projects. When contractors, engineers, and suppliers from different countries reference the same standards and units, it becomes significantly easier to verify that materials meet the necessary specifications, regardless of where they were manufactured or tested.

In conclusion, the combination of standardized testing procedures like SCPA and universal measurement units such as MPa represents a cornerstone of modern engineering practice. This system ensures that materials are evaluated consistently, promoting safety, reliability, and international cooperation in construction and manufacturing sectors worldwide.

# Patent Claim Summary
## Chain Guide/Tensioner Component with Semi-Crystalline Polyamide Surface Layer

### Field of Invention
This invention relates to chain guide and tensioner components for power transmission systems, particularly timing chain systems in internal combustion engines, having improved wear resistance and friction characteristics under oil-lubricated operating conditions.

---

### Claim 1 (Independent Claim)

A chain guide/tensioner component for guiding or tensioning a power transmission chain, comprising:

**(a)** a substrate body defining a chain-contacting surface configured to engage a moving chain under oil-lubricated conditions; and

**(b)** a surface layer disposed on at least the chain-contacting surface of said substrate body, said surface layer comprising a semi-crystalline polyamide resin,

wherein said surface layer exhibits:
- (i) a tensile modulus of elasticity in the range of **1,500 MPa to 4,500 MPa**, as measured according to ISO 527-1/2 (or ASTM D638) at 23°C;
- (ii) a coefficient of dynamic friction of less than **0.15** when tested against a mating steel chain component under oil-lubricated conditions at a temperature range of 80°C to 130°C; and
- (iii) a degree of crystallinity of at least **20%** by weight, as determined by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC),

whereby the surface layer provides reduced sliding friction and improved wear resistance during oscillating or sliding chain contact while maintaining sufficient rigidity to resist deformation under chain tension loads.

---

### Claim 2 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said semi-crystalline polyamide is selected from the group consisting of polyamide 46 (PA46), polyamide 66 (PA66), polyamide 6 (PA6), polyamide 610, polyamide 12, and blends or copolymers thereof.

### Claim 3 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said surface layer further comprises a reinforcing filler selected from glass fibers, carbon fibers, aramid fibers, or combinations thereof, present in an amount of **10% to 40% by weight** based on the total weight of the surface layer.

### Claim 4 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said surface layer further comprises a solid lubricant additive selected from polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), molybdenum disulfide, graphite, or silicone oil, present in an amount of **1% to 15% by weight**.

### Claim 5 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said surface layer has a thickness in the range of **0.5 mm to 3.0 mm**.

### Claim 6 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said tensile modulus of elasticity is in the range of **2,000 MPa to 3,500 MPa**.

### Claim 7 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said coefficient of dynamic friction is less than **0.10** under said oil-lubricated conditions.

### Claim 8 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said substrate body comprises a metal selected from aluminum, aluminum alloy, or steel, and said surface layer is bonded to said substrate body by injection molding, insert molding, or mechanical interlocking features.

### Claim 9 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said semi-crystalline polyamide has a melting point of at least **200°C**, as determined by DSC.

### Claim 10 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein the component is selected from the group consisting of a chain guide shoe, a tensioner arm, a fixed guide, and a pivoting guide for a timing chain drive system of an internal combustion engine.

### Claim 11 (Dependent)
The component of claim 1, wherein said surface layer further exhibits a water absorption rate of less than **1.5%** by weight after 24 hours of immersion at 23°C, thereby minimizing dimensional swelling under humid or oil-exposed engine operating conditions.

### Claim 12 (Independent - Method Claim)
A method of manufacturing a chain guide/tensioner component, comprising:
**(a)** providing a substrate body having a chain-contacting surface;
**(b)** forming a surface layer on said chain-contacting surface using a semi-crystalline polyamide composition having a tensile modulus of 1,500 MPa to 4,500 MPa; and
**(c)** curing or solidifying said surface layer to achieve a crystallinity of at least 20% by weight,
wherein the resulting surface layer exhibits a coefficient of dynamic friction of less than 0.15 against a steel chain under oil-lubricated conditions.

---

### Notes for Prosecution
- Consider narrower dependent claims specifying exact PA46/PA66 grades (e.g., Stanyl®, Zytel® HTN) for commercial embodiment protection.
- Friction coefficient testing protocol (e.g., pin-on-disk vs. actual chain rig) should be specified in the specification to support enablement.
- Consider claiming synergistic combination of modulus range + friction range as inventive over prior art teaching either property alone.

# TECHNICAL FIELD

The present disclosure relates generally to sliding elements used in power train drive systems, and more particularly to sliding elements formed from a polymeric matrix material for use in guiding, tensioning, or supporting a lubricated chain in an engine or transmission environment. The disclosure further relates to chain guides, tensioner arms, and chain slippers incorporating such polymeric sliding elements, as well as methods of manufacturing the same.

# SUMMARY

Power train drive systems, such as those employed in internal combustion engines, transmissions, and various industrial machinery, commonly utilize chains to transmit rotational motion and torque between two or more rotating members, such as sprockets mounted on a crankshaft, camshaft, balance shaft, or other rotating shafts. To maintain proper chain tension, reduce noise, and minimize wear during operation, such drive systems typically incorporate one or more sliding elements, including chain guides and tensioner arms, against which the chain slides or engages during operation of the drive system.

Conventional sliding elements are often formed from polymeric materials due to their favorable wear resistance, noise dampening properties, and cost-effectiveness relative to metallic components. However, sliding elements used in lubricated chain environments, such as those found in engine timing chain systems, are subjected to a combination of mechanical loading, frictional heating, and continuous exposure to lubricants such as engine oil. Over extended periods of operation, exposure to lubricants at elevated temperatures can lead to degradation of certain polymeric materials, including swelling, softening, oxidation, or loss of mechanical properties such as tensile strength, wear resistance, and dimensional stability. Additionally, the additive packages present in modern lubricants, including detergents, dispersants, anti-wear agents, and viscosity modifiers, may interact with polymeric matrix materials in ways that accelerate degradation or negatively impact the frictional characteristics of the sliding surface.

Furthermore, sliding elements in power train drive systems must withstand repeated cyclic loading from contact with the moving chain over the operational life of the engine or transmission, which may span hundreds of thousands of kilometers or hours of operation. This necessitates a sliding element material that not only exhibits low friction and wear against the chain material, which is typically metallic, but also maintains dimensional and mechanical stability throughout prolonged lubricant exposure and thermal cycling. Conventional polymeric sliding elements may exhibit inconsistent performance in this regard, particularly as engine operating temperatures increase and lubricant formulations evolve to meet more stringent efficiency and emissions requirements.

There remains a need in the art for a sliding element formed from a polymeric matrix material that exhibits improved resistance to lubricant-induced degradation, enhanced wear resistance against a chain surface, and maintained mechanical integrity over extended service life, while remaining cost-effective and suitable for high-volume manufacturing processes such as injection molding.

The present disclosure addresses these and other needs by providing a sliding element for use in a power train drive system having a lubricated chain, wherein the sliding element comprises a polymeric matrix material configured to provide a sliding surface for contacting the chain during operation. In accordance with various embodiments, the polymeric matrix material may comprise a thermoplastic resin, including but not limited to a polyamide, a polyphenylene sulfide, a polyoxymethylene, a polyketone, or combinations thereof, selected to provide a desired balance of mechanical strength, wear resistance, and chemical resistance to lubricants.

In certain embodiments, the polymeric matrix material may be combined with one or more reinforcing agents, such as fibrous reinforcements including glass fibers, carbon fibers, or aramid fibers, to enhance the mechanical properties of the sliding element, including tensile strength, flexural modulus, and creep resistance under sustained loading conditions encountered during chain engagement.

In further embodiments, the polymeric matrix material may include one or more solid lubricant additives, such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), molybdenum disulfide, graphite, or combinations thereof, dispersed within the matrix to reduce the coefficient of friction at the sliding surface and thereby reduce wear of both the sliding element and the chain during operation.

According to additional aspects of the present disclosure, the sliding element may be configured as a chain guide, a tensioner arm, or a chain slipper, each having a body portion formed from the polymeric matrix material and a sliding surface configured to engage the chain along at least a portion of its length. The body portion may further include a plurality of mounting features, such as apertures, bosses, or pivot points, configured to secure the sliding element to a housing or bracket within the power train drive system.

In accordance with certain embodiments, the sliding element may be formed via an injection molding process, wherein the polymeric matrix material, along with any reinforcing agents or additives, is introduced into a mold cavity corresponding to the desired shape of the sliding element, including the sliding surface and any mounting features.

The sliding elements described herein provide numerous advantages over conventional polymeric sliding elements, including improved resistance to degradation caused by prolonged exposure to lubricants, enhanced wear resistance against metallic chain components, and improved dimensional stability over a range of operating temperatures typically encountered in power train drive systems. These and other advantages, features, and objects of the present disclosure will become apparent from the following detailed description and accompanying drawings.
